result:
I accepted round 379 and wrote the round 380 task: PERF-12a, the first of two stages of the chunked WAV export. The decision is **CONTINUE**. I changed no app code; the store tree is clean.

**Round 379 accepted.** C passed it with `browserVerified` true and 0 bugs, and gate 379 published `ed634d5`. From the gate review:
- Two Lows go to the deferred polish list: GATE379-L3 and A-R379-REVIEW-L1.
- The other findings were info only and are closed.
- The architecture note is recorded as signal SIG-R379-GATE-ACTIONS-CONTEXT. It is the eighth unanswered echo of the leaf-plumbing checkpoint; RETRO 384 remains its deadline.

**Why PERF-12a now:**
- REGRESSION is not due until 2026-11-08 (2 days since the last one; the rule needs 3).
- VideoDock and Lane (PERF-11c-iii-d/e) wait for the architecture checkpoint, and PERF-11b waits for Saba.
- I re-measured the export cost in the browser first. Today's HEAD keeps +65 MiB of page memory during a one-clip export (+130 MiB for two clips), and has 171–304 ms long tasks at 6× CPU throttling. Almost all of that comes from the `getChannelData().slice()` copies and the WAV bytes being returned to the page.

**What round 380 does.** The export keeps its single render. The page copies the result out in 65,536-frame chunks and sends them to the WAV worker one at a time, and the worker returns a finished Blob. A applies three patches I prepared, then migrates the old export tests to rows SW1–SW7 with an old-to-new row map, runs 8 unit mutants and writes doc 246.

**What I checked on the sketch:**
- **Same file:** exported WAVs were byte-identical to HEAD at both viewports, for the whole project, two clips, a time selection and Master at +6 dB.
- **Gap:** the Master +6 dB step doesn't clip on either tree, so the browser never exercises the overload text. Unit rows and mutants cover it instead.
- **Perf:** with the four budget rows switched to asserts, peak page memory dropped to 0.1 / 0.2 MiB (limit 5) and the 6× long tasks to 0 ms (limit 100), with wall time no worse than HEAD. Both perf mutants make those rows fail.
- **Unit tests:** 475 of 495 pass. The 20 failures are exactly the old-protocol rows A must migrate.
- **Consults:** `tech-lead` found one real bug (a throwing progress callback stalled the export) and two smaller issues; all three are fixed in the dispatched sketch. I kept one chunk in flight instead of `performance-optimizer`'s suggested two, because wall time was already no worse than HEAD.

C verifies against HEAD in the browser at both viewports: byte identity, Cancel, MP3, the auth guard and the perf spec.

**Question for Saba (SABA-Q-PERF12B-TOLERANCE).** The perf plan promises a chunked export that is "bit-exact" with a full render. `tech-lead` says that isn't achievable for stage 12b's 30-second windowed renders. I wrote the question in Georgian in `user-review/questions-perf12b.md`: may it differ by at most 1 LSB at 24-bit near window edges, with identical peak and clipped counts? It blocks nothing now; 12b can be built and measured, but its tolerance asserts and publication wait for his answer.

**Next after 380:** REGRESSION-2026-11-08, then PERF-12b, then VideoDock and Lane, then RETRO 384, then the rest of the queue unchanged.

The project agents I consulted were `tech-lead` and `performance-optimizer`. The advisor was available and was consulted before I chose the approach and again before handover.
